subject: CDBG Program Public Hearing
overview: The Office of Planning, Development and Sustainability held a public hearing to review recent accomplishments of the Community Development Block Grant program and to solicit resident input for future funding cycles. Staff detailed completed infrastructure projects and affordable housing initiatives while outlining upcoming improvements for city parks and sidewalks.

items.title: CDBG Program Overview and Eligibility
items.summary: Ashley Williams defined the program's primary goal as benefiting low- and moderate-income Medford residents through federal HUD grants for public facilities, housing, and social services.

items.title: Program Year Timeline and Reporting
items.summary: Staff reviewed the annual cycle for grant applications and the current preparation of the Consolidated Annual Performance and Evaluation Report (CAPER).

items.title: Infrastructure and Public Facility Accomplishments
items.summary: Completed projects included utility and roadway improvements on Prescott, Alston, and Cottage Streets, as well as ADA upgrades at Tufts Pool and fire station renovations.

items.title: Affordable Housing and Public Service Updates
items.summary: The department progressed a draft housing production plan and allocated 15% of grant funding to support local social service agencies like the Council on Aging and ABCD.

items.title: Upcoming Public Works and Park Projects
items.summary: Future priorities include sidewalk improvements on Pinker Street and renovations to Morrison, Logan, and Brooks Parks, including a new natural play area and community garden beds.

items.title: Public Comment and Inquiries
items.summary: Staff addressed resident questions regarding affordable housing lotteries, the development status of 551 Winthrop Street, and the feasibility of attracting a new grocery store to the city.
